account: It is just before eight on day 1, and I am in my office for the morning appointment. I read and returned the appointment book. Today includes a ten o'clock grain inspection at the mill, lunch at home, council letters at one, daily tea at the neighbour's dockside cottage at three, and office business at four thirty. The secretary has just arrived and reports visiting the mill yesterday evening and early today without finding the miller. That is worth following up at the inspection, but I do not know why the miller was absent or whether anything is wrong. Neither the baker nor the neighbour reported firsthand concerns. Yesterday the neighbour mentioned unconfirmed rumours of a celebration or bridge changes; neither of us had evidence, and the baker reportedly knew of no celebration. I also saw a lantern appear beside a great-hall table yesterday, but do not know who placed it or why. At present I have no evidence connecting these observations or suggesting an unusual organized activity. The secretary is helping keep appointments and gather information; the neighbour is now outside near the town hall, though I do not know the purpose of that visit.
